title: On dispositions: real agreement; only a logomachy remains
source_text: LVII. Itaque cum Protestantes non simpliciter negent ante justificationem conditio-nes quasdam, & dispositiones morales praerequiri, quo nihil amplius hac in parte exigit Ecclesia Romana, nec Pontificii velint has dispositiones rationem habere causae efficientis, vel meritoriae, respectu nostrae justificationis, a quo hic unice Protestantes abhorrent: hinc concludere licet, nullam inter utrosque de istis dispositionibus con-troversiam realem existere, sed solummodo quandam logomachiam, quae, formularum varia interpretatione sublata, facile tolli potest.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore since the Protestants do not simply deny that certain conditions and moral dispositions are prerequisite before justification—than which the Roman Church demands nothing further in this part—and since the Papists do not wish these dispositions to have the role of an efficient or meritorious cause with respect to our justification, from which alone the Protestants here shrink: hence one may conclude that no real controversy exists between them about these dispositions, but only a certain dispute about words, which, once the varying interpretation of formulas is removed, can easily be taken away.
pass_b_english: Since Protestants allow moral conditions/dispositions before justification, and Rome does not make them efficient/meritorious causes—the one point Protestants solely reject—no real controversy remains, only a logomachy.

choices.why: Irenic close: verbal not real clash on dispositions.
